column1: What is the 'observer effect' in performance measurement, and why does `rdtsc` exemplify it?
column2: Instrumentation itself consumes cycles and alters execution behavior. `rdtsc` serializes out-of-order pipelines, forcing prior instructions to complete before capturing the timestamp, so the measured duration includes stall cycles induced by the measurement itself.

column1: Define Big-O, Big-Omega, and Big-Theta notation formally.
column2: Big-O: T(n)=O(f(n)) if ∃ c,n₀ such that T(n) ≤ c·f(n) for n≥n₀ (upper bound). Big-Omega: T(n)=Ω(f(n)) if T(n) ≥ c·f(n) for n≥n₀ (lower bound). Big-Theta: T(n)=Θ(f(n)) when both O(f(n)) and Ω(f(n)) hold (tight bound).

column1: What is the proven lower bound for comparison-based sorting, and why does it matter?
column2: Ω(n log n). It proves no comparison sort can beat n log n worst-case, forcing engineers toward non-comparison algorithms (radix sort, counting sort) when asymptotically better performance is required.

column1: List the approximate latency figures for each level of the memory hierarchy (L1, L2, L3, local DRAM, remote NUMA).
column2: L1: 4–5 cycles (~1.5 ns); L2: 12–15 cycles; L3: 30–50 cycles; local DRAM: 60–80 ns; remote NUMA memory: 120–200+ ns.

column1: Why is the cache line size of 64 bytes significant for memory access, even for small reads?
column2: The cache line is the atomic unit of transfer between memory hierarchy levels. A single load miss pulls in all 64 bytes regardless of how much data is actually needed, meaning spatial locality determines whether that transfer is productive or wasted bandwidth/capacity.

column1: What is false sharing, and how is it mitigated in C++?
column2: False sharing occurs when two independent variables reside on the same cache line; writes by different threads to each variable generate full MESI coherence traffic as if they shared state. Mitigated via `alignas(std::hardware_destructive_interference_size)` to pad/separate fields onto distinct cache lines.

column1: Explain the MESI protocol's role when core B writes to a cache line held Modified by core A.
column2: The hardware must invalidate core A's copy, force a writeback to L3/main memory, transfer the line to core B, and transition it to Modified on core B — a round trip costing roughly 50–300 cycles (~100 ns at 3 GHz).

column1: Why can't network optimization reduce transcontinental latency below the propagation delay floor?
column2: Signal propagation in fiber travels at ~200,000 km/s (≈2/3 speed of light due to refractive index). This sets a physical minimum round-trip time (e.g., ~56ms NY–London) that no software, protocol, or bandwidth optimization can circumvent.

column1: Distinguish network bandwidth from latency and explain why increasing bandwidth often fails to improve small-payload request performance.
column2: Bandwidth is the data transfer rate once transmission begins; latency is the time before the first bit arrives. For small payloads (e.g., 1KB), transmission time is microseconds while RTT latency is milliseconds — so doubling bandwidth yields negligible end-to-end improvement since latency dominates.

column1: What was Knuth's actual, commonly misquoted statement about premature optimization?
column2: "We should forget about small efficiencies, say about 97% of the time: premature optimization is the root of all evil. Yet we should not pass up our opportunities in that critical 3%." The nuance: avoid unfocused optimization absent measurement, but do seize measured, high-impact opportunities.

column1: Why do modern processors and compilers reorder memory operations, and what problem does this create for concurrent code?
column2: Reordering (by CPU, compiler, and interconnect) optimizes performance but breaks naive assumptions about program order across threads, creating data races and requiring explicit memory model contracts (fences, atomics) to restore necessary ordering guarantees.

column1: What hardware mechanism explains why a mutex is 'slow,' according to coherence-centric analysis?
column2: It's not the lock primitive itself but the cache coherence traffic generated by contention on the lock variable's cache line — invalidations and line transfers across cores cost tens to hundreds of cycles, dominating execution time under contention.
